supported_claims.text: The dossier supports an account of 系 as a hand holding connected silk, interpreted as binding or connection, but presents it as a paleographic interpretation rather than a settled reconstruction.

A distinct received 說文 analysis parses 系 as 糸 plus 丿, with 丿 supplying sound. Another account interprets seal-script 丿 as a reduced hand and questions that phonetic analysis; the dossier does not resolve the disagreement.
系 is explicitly recorded as a phonetic element in 係. The account of 係 separately describes 人 and 糸 as binding a person with a cord, and records its early verb use.

系’s recorded uses include oracle-bone ritual and place/state names, later bronze personal names, and a Warring States use writing 奚. These reported uses do not establish dated stages in the meanings ‘thread,’ ‘lineage’ or ‘system.’

A source proposes an extension from connection to lineage and cites a Han-dynasty text example. The dossier does not establish intermediate chronology or a historical development to the modern gloss ‘system.’
系, 係 and 繫 have related graphic and lexical records, but the dossier does not establish that 系 is a regular historical simplification of 繫 or specify when the graphs were interchangeable.

For 系 and 係, the supplied Baxter–Sagart rows give different Old Chinese forms (*[m]-kˤek-s and *kˤek-s) and Middle Chinese transcriptions (hejH and kejH). Sources attest 系’s phonetic role in 係, but the precise historical sound relation is not resolved.
The curated seal-script images are modern redrawings rather than artifact photographs and do not by themselves establish a chronological sequence.

disagreements.text: 系’s formation is disputed: the received 說文 account treats 丿 as a phonetic alongside 糸, while the paleographic interpretation treats it as a reduced hand in a hand-and-connected-silk picture. A separate proposal identifies 系 as an early form of 攣. The dossier does not adjudicate these accounts.

The dossier describes 系, 係 and 繫 as historically interchangeable in some uses, but also records a proposed simplification from 繫 to 系 and a variant/counterpart listing. The evidence supplied does not establish a single graphic chronology or the extent of interchange.

limitations.text: The earliest inscriptional forms of 系 are not independently dated in the supplied research. Reported early graph uses cannot be treated as dated attestations of particular lexical senses.
The lineage extension is proposed, but its intermediate semantic history is not documented here; the gloss ‘system’ has no supported historical sequence in this dossier.
係’s later connection and copular uses are recorded, but their earliest dated attestations and transitions from binding are not established.
繫’s cited tie, confinement, hanging, concern and relation senses do not establish their chronological order or a graphic simplification into 系.

Exact Baxter–Sagart rows were supplied as local observations, and official Unicode Unihan records could not be accessed; those materials are not independently verified through the cited online records in this research.
No glyph pixels were visually inspected; the supplied images are described as modern seal-script redraws.
